clue.text: Coming to it, stay put

definitions.meaning: to come to a halt is to come to a complete stop, so 'it' stands for that stop
to remain motionless on one's feet, not moving at all

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the noun for a complete halt (traffic comes to one); the other is the verb phrase for keeping motionless, written as one word.

clue.text: "It cannot thus be long, the — of nature Will not sustain it " (A and C.)

definitions.text: "It cannot thus be long, the — of nature Will not sustain it " (A and C.)

parts.words: "It cannot thus be long, the — of nature Will not sustain it " (A and C.)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation from Shakespeare's Antony and Cleopatra, Act 1, where the missing word means the body's flanks or frame

explanation.definitionFit: In the play the word means the body's frame or flanks, which cannot bear such grief for long.

clue.text: Find out how "sure" may be defined

definitions.meaning: to discover or establish for certain
split as two words it reads '...', a gloss of the word sure

explanation.definitionFit: The word means to discover or establish; split as two words it gives a synonym phrase for confident.

clue.text: His films were a big draw

definitions.text: His films were a big draw

parts.words: His films were a big draw
parts.note: a big draw is a popular attraction, but these films were also literally drawn as cartoons

explanation.definitionFit: Walt Disney's animated films were hand-drawn cartoons and also hugely popular.

clue.text: The caddy gets the benefit of his labours

definitions.text: The caddy gets the benefit of his labours

parts.words: The caddy gets the benefit of his labours
parts.note: the caddy is not a golfer's helper but the tin for storing leaves for brewing

explanation.definitionFit: A tea planter grows the leaf that ends up stored in a tea caddy.

clue.text: Would you strike a false note on this instrument?

definitions.text: Would you strike a false note on this instrument?

parts.words: Would you strike a false note on this instrument?
parts.note: striking a false note suggests a lie; the harp-like instrument's name sounds like a teller of untruths

explanation.definitionFit: A lyre is an ancient plucked stringed instrument, its name sounding like 'liar'.

clue.text: He makes a belated start

indicators.note: the start of the words 'a belated' gives a short name, so the beginning of that run is the source

explanation.surface: Someone gets going late in the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start' means the opening letters of 'a belated'; 'makes' just links. The man is the Biblical son of Adam, killed by his brother Cain.
explanation.definitionFit: Abel, second son of Adam and Eve in Genesis, is a man, so the pronoun stands for him.

clue.text: The beautiful Italian.

parts.note: the Italian word for beautiful, in its feminine form, and also a woman's name

explanation.definitionFit: Bella is Italian for beautiful (feminine), and is also an Italian girl's name.

clue.text: It is held up for inspection

definitions.text: It is held up for inspection

parts.words: It is held up for inspection
parts.note: held up suggests a delay, but these eyeglasses on a handle are lifted to the eyes to look at things

explanation.definitionFit: A lorgnette is a pair of spectacles on a long handle, raised to the eyes to look at someone.

clue.text: Prepare cutlets for "that sinking feeling "!

indicators.note: preparing the meat means working it into a new form, so the letters of cutlets are reworked

explanation.walkthrough: 'Prepare' rearranges CUTLETS. To scuttle a ship is to sink it deliberately.
explanation.definitionFit: To scuttle is to sink a vessel on purpose by holing it, so the sinking is the sense.

clue.text: Ships do not undergo their trials in them.

definitions.text: Ships do not undergo their trials in them.

parts.words: Ships do not undergo their trials in them.
parts.note: a ship's sea trials happen out at sea, not in harbour basins; but the accused in court undergo their trials standing in a different kind of enclosure with the same name

explanation.definitionFit: Docks are harbour basins where ships berth, and a dock is also the enclosure where a prisoner stands in court.

clue.text: The nature of Antony's requested loan

definitions.text: The nature of Antony's requested loan

parts.words: The nature of Antony's requested loan
parts.note: in Julius Caesar Mark Antony begins 'Friends, Romans, countrymen, lend me your ears', so the loan he asks for is of the ear

explanation.definitionFit: Auricular means relating to the ear, and the ears are what Antony asks the crowd to lend him.

clue.text: Who will may hear his story told, said Browning

definitions.text: Who will may hear his story told, said Browning

parts.words: Who will may hear his story told, said Browning
parts.note: Robert Browning's long poem opens with the line 'Who will, may hear ... story told', naming its hero, a medieval Italian troubadour

explanation.definitionFit: Sordello is the title figure of Browning's 1840 poem, whose first line promises his story to whoever will listen.

clue.text: Music for a tug-of-war

definitions.meaning: a tune or passage of melody
the hard pull and tension felt on the rope by each team

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a melody or tune, and also a heavy pull or tension such as a rope under load.

clue.text: Not surprising that he rose to the height of his profession

definitions.text: Not surprising that he rose to the height of his profession

parts.words: Not surprising that he rose to the height of his profession
parts.note: the American poet's surname splits into words meaning a tall man, so reaching great heights was to be expected

explanation.definitionFit: Henry Wadsworth Longfellow rose to the top of poetry, and his name reads as 'tall chap'.

clue.text: It's striking when friends stage a come-back

indicators.note: making a come-back means turning around, so the word for friends is read from its end to its start

parts.note: pals are friends

explanation.surface: A theatrical reunion of old friends makes an impression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stage a come-back' turns PALS round. 'It's striking' is the definition: a blow with the open hand is a striking act.
explanation.definitionFit: A smack with the open hand is an act of hitting, so something that is striking in the literal sense.

clue.text: In good all-round shape

parts.note: in good shape suggests fitness, but all-round shape is literally the shape of a ball

explanation.definitionFit: Spherical means shaped like a ball, round in every direction.

clue.text: Ruin a continental party

parts.note: un is the French for a, French being a continental language
a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: A party in Europe goes badly wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'continental' signals a European language: French UN for 'a'.
explanation.definitionFit: To undo someone is to bring about their downfall, so it can mean to wreck or destroy.

clue.text: Kipling's was one that failed

parts.note: Rudyard Kipling's first novel was 'The ... that Failed' (1891), about a painter going blind

explanation.definitionFit: Kipling's novel title names a lamp's glow or illumination that went out, as the painter's sight does.

clue.text: Hardy tree

parts.note: a tree that is hardy suggests a tough species, but it is the tree of Thomas Hardy's novel 'Under the ... Tree'

explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Hardy's novel is Under the Greenwood Tree, a greenwood being a forest in leaf.

clue.text: La Butterfly's first name?

parts.note: the red admiral and painted lady belong to a butterfly genus that is also a woman's forename, invented by Swift

explanation.definitionFit: Vanessa is the genus of red admirals and painted ladies, and a woman's name coined by Jonathan Swift.

clue.text: Boy meets girl returning from the dye-works ?

parts.note: a boy is a he, a male

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the girl's name is read from its end to its start

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A romantic encounter at a factory where cloth is coloured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns the girl's name round. The question mark marks the definition as a hint: henna is a product a dye-maker would turn out, not the works itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The reddish colouring made from a shrub's leaves is a product a dye-maker would supply, used on hair and skin.

clue.text: They're in your clutch

parts.note: a clutch is the set of a bird's laid ova sitting in the nest, not something gripped in the hand or a car pedal

explanation.definitionFit: A clutch is a batch laid at one time by a hen or other bird, made up of these.

clue.text: She's one of the best

indicators.note: one part of the words 'the best' holds the goddess, so the letters are drawn from inside that phrase

explanation.surface: A woman is praised as among the finest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one of' signals letters taken from inside 'the best'. Hebe is the Greek goddess of youth and cupbearer to the gods.
explanation.definitionFit: Hebe, Greek goddess of youth, is female, so the pronoun stands for her.

clue.text: "In Vishnu-land what" (Browning)

parts.note: a line of Browning's 'Waring' asks 'In Vishnu-land what ...?', meaning the earthly form a Hindu god takes

explanation.definitionFit: An avatar is the incarnation of a Hindu deity such as Vishnu in bodily form.

clue.text: Does the sculptor find respite in such work?

definitions.text: Does the sculptor find respite in such work?

parts.words: Does the sculptor find respite in such work?
parts.note: one word means both respite from strain and a carving whose figures stand out from a flat background

explanation.definitionFit: Relief is easing of distress, and in sculpture it is carving raised from a flat surface.

clue.text: Chesterton's flowery. Lord remembered Shakespeare

parts.note: in G. K. Chesterton's poem 'The Shakespeare Memorial', a peer with a flower's name 'remembered Shakespeare with a start'

explanation.definitionFit: Lord Lilac is the peer of Chesterton's comic poem, and lilac is a flowering shrub.

clue.text: Departures — by man's free will ?

definitions.meaning: what someone hands on by will, bequests left behind

explanation.definitionFit: The word can mean acts of going away, and also what is left over or bequeathed by a will.

clue.text: A war-time shirtmaker

parts.note: the First World War music-hall song 'Sister ...'s Sewing Shirts for Soldiers' names her

explanation.walkthrough: The song 'Sister Susie's Sewing Shirts for Soldiers' (1914) was a British music-hall hit of the First World War.
explanation.definitionFit: Sister Susie of the 1914 song sews shirts for soldiers during the war.

clue.text: Artist bereft of land, but not of vision

definitions.note: the definition names the quality, the answer the person who has it: 'but not of vision' says he still has it

indicators.note: bereft of means robbed of, so the named word is removed from the painter's name

parts.note: Sir Edwin Landseer was a Victorian painter, known for animals and the Trafalgar Square lions
taken as written

explanation.surface: A painter who has lost his estate keeps his imagination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bereft of land' strips LAND from LANDSEER. 'but not of vision' says the man that is left still has vision.
explanation.definitionFit: A seer is a prophet, one gifted with visions of the future.

clue.text: No striking while the iron's hot with this

definitions.text: No striking while the iron's hot with this

parts.words: No striking while the iron's hot with this
parts.note: the proverb says strike while the iron is hot; a blade used to strike in combat is unheated metal

explanation.definitionFit: Cold steel means bladed weapons such as swords and bayonets, the metal being unheated.

clue.text: His wife and his nipper were identical

definitions.text: His wife and his nipper were identical

parts.words: His wife and his nipper were identical
parts.note: in Dickens's Dombey and Son the maid Susan Nipper marries the amiable Mr ... so his wife is his Nipper

explanation.definitionFit: Mr Toots of Dombey and Son marries Susan Nipper, so his wife and his Nipper are one woman.

clue.text: Not the fish for fast-days, by the sound of it

definitions.text: Not the fish for fast-days, by the sound of it

parts.words: Not the fish for fast-days, by the sound of it
parts.note: a pike's old name sounds like the word for slack or free, the opposite of fast

explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' here means secure, not abstaining; the fish's name sounds like 'loose', which is not fast.
explanation.definitionFit: A luce is an old name for a pike, especially a full-grown one.

clue.text: Once a defence against gatecrashers

parts.note: a castle's hinged bridge over the moat was raised to keep attackers out of the gate

explanation.definitionFit: A castle's raisable bridge over a moat kept attackers from reaching the gatehouse.
